evidence: Michael J. Kennedy wrote Ireland and the League of Nations, Guarding Neutral Ireland and the Troubles article (3/19 listed thesis citations). The Jacobin titles are Michael L. Kennedy's; the music books are the music critic's; The Assiniboines was edited by Michael Stephen Kennedy; Internationalism is Michael D. Kennedy's.

The key's ISNI/VIAF identify Robert Ryal Miller: Arms across the Border, Juan Alvarado, Captain Richardson, Shamrock and Sword and Lew Wallace account for 6/19 listed thesis citations. Native America (6) is Robert J. Miller's; Vietnam and Beyond is Robert Hopkins Miller's; Aid as Peacemaker belongs to the Parliamentary Centre's Robert Miller.

Hidden History of the Korean War, Trial of Socrates and its translations, The Truman Era and The Haunted Fifties are the journalist's. Hypothesis versus Fact credits I. R. Stone; Arnold fitz Thedmar credits Ian William Stone. The journalist dominates; the Eduardo Gallegos Mancera item remains uncertain.

Copper for America, Technological Change and the British Iron Industry, the automobile histories and industrial-history articles are Charles K. Hyde's (14/20 listed thesis citations). The six international-law entries, including The Nationality Act of 1940, Eastern Greenland and the polar-sovereignty titles, belong to Charles Cheney Hyde.

The Indo-European and Ulster archaeology titles are James Patrick Mallory's (14/20 listed thesis citations). Social Credit and the Federal Power in Canada (4), The Appointment of the Governor General (1) and Biography, History, and Social Science in Canada (1) are J. R. Mallory's.

The Guelph historian's CV confirms Resisting Manchukuo, Intoxicating Manchuria, Empire and Environment and Writing Opium (10/21 listed thesis citations). A History of Dams is Norman Alfred Fisher Smith's; The Journal Men is Irving Norman Smith's; New Studies in the Philosophy of Descartes is Norman Kemp Smith's. The remaining older entries are outside the key's work.

The Precariat, A Precariat Charter and the labour, commons and basic-income works are Guy Standing's (21/22 listed thesis citations). The Claudian Invasion of Britain and the Cult of Victoria Britannica is explicitly credited to Giles Standing by the journal.

From Nicaea to Chalcedon, Biblical Exegesis, the Cambridge histories and the other patristic works belong to Frances Margaret Young (18/19 listed thesis citations). The First Edmund Berkeley in Virginia (1933) is by Frances Berkeley Young, a separate author.

The Divided Welfare State, Winner-Take-All Politics, The Great Risk Shift and the institutional/social-policy works are Jacob S. Hacker's (20/22 listed thesis citations). Trends and Determinants of Adult Mortality is J. David Hacker's, as is the Haines coauthored contribution to Navigating Time and Space in Population Studies.

Die Homosexualität des Mannes und des Weibes, Die Transvestiten/Transvestites, Berlins drittes Geschlecht and the other sexological/historical works are Magnus Hirschfeld's (approximately 26/27 listed thesis citations). The Effect of News on Bond Prices credits Mary Hirshfeld/Hirschfeld with Douglas Elmendorf and David Weil.
